# COMPLETE LOGIC FOR MULTI-HORIZON ENSEMBLE

This document outlines the complete logic structure for creating 3 separate ensemble models (1Q, 6M, 1Y).
Once you show me your actual data format, I'll adjust the column names accordingly.

---

## OVERVIEW: Multi-Horizon Strategy

**Problem:** We need to make predictions at 3 different time horizons:
- **1-Quarter (3 months)**: Rebalance every quarter
- **6-Month (2 quarters)**: Rebalance every 6 months  
- **1-Year (4 quarters)**: Rebalance annually

**Solution:** Create 3 separate LSEI ensemble models, one for each horizon

**Why Separate?** Because:
1. Models may perform differently at different horizons
2. A model good at short-term forecasting may not be good at long-term
3. We want to learn optimal weights specific to each forecasting task

```
3. PCR Training Predictions (pcr_train_predictions.csv):
   - date
   - actual_1q, actual_6m, actual_1y
   - pcr_forecast_1q, pcr_forecast_6m, pcr_forecast_1y

4. RF Test Predictions (rf_test_predictions.csv):
   - Same structure as training
   
5. XGBoost Test Predictions (xgb_test_predictions.csv):
   - Same structure as training
   
6. PCR Test Predictions (pcr_test_predictions.csv):
   - Same structure as training
```

# PART 2: LOAD & COMBINE TRAINING DATA

## Step 2.1: Load Training Predictions

```r
# PSEUDO-CODE LOGIC:

# Load RF
rf_train <- read_csv("rf_train_predictions.csv") %>%
  select(date, 
         actual_1q, actual_6m, actual_1y,
         rf_forecast_1q, rf_forecast_6m, rf_forecast_1y)

# Load XGBoost  
xgb_train <- read_csv("xgb_train_predictions.csv") %>%
  select(date,
         xgb_forecast_1q, xgb_forecast_6m, xgb_forecast_1y)
         
# Load PCR
pcr_train <- read_csv("pcr_train_predictions.csv") %>%
  select(date,
         pcr_forecast_1q, pcr_forecast_6m, pcr_forecast_1y)
```

## Step 2.2: Combine Training Data

```r
# Merge all predictions by date
train_combined <- rf_train %>%
  left_join(xgb_train, by = "date") %>%
  left_join(pcr_train, by = "date")

# Result structure:
# date | actual_1q | actual_6m | actual_1y | 
#      | rf_forecast_1q | rf_forecast_6m | rf_forecast_1y |
#      | xgb_forecast_1q | xgb_forecast_6m | xgb_forecast_1y |
#      | pcr_forecast_1q | pcr_forecast_6m | pcr_forecast_1y
```

---

# PART 3: CREATE 3 SEPARATE ENSEMBLE MODELS

## ENSEMBLE 1: 1-Quarter Horizon

### Step 3.1.1: Prepare Data for 1Q Ensemble

```r
cat("\n=== CREATING 1-QUARTER ENSEMBLE ===\n")

# Prediction matrix: 3 models x N observations
X_train_1q <- train_combined %>%
  select(rf_forecast_1q, xgb_forecast_1q, pcr_forecast_1q) %>%
  as.matrix()

colnames(X_train_1q) <- c("RF", "XGBoost", "PCR")

# Actual returns (target)
y_train_1q <- train_combined$actual_1q

n_models <- 3
```

### Step 3.1.2: Set Up Constraints for 1Q

```r
# Equality: sum(weights) = 1
E <- matrix(1, nrow = 1, ncol = n_models)
f <- 1

# Inequality: all weights >= 0
G <- diag(n_models)
h <- rep(0, n_models)
```

### Step 3.1.3: Solve LSEI for 1Q Weights

```r
# Minimize ||X*weights - y||^2 subject to constraints
lsei_1q <- lsei(A = X_train_1q, B = y_train_1q, E = E, F = f, G = G, H = h)

# Extract weights
weights_1q <- lsei_1q$X
names(weights_1q) <- c("RF", "XGBoost", "PCR")

cat("1Q Ensemble Weights:\n")
print(weights_1q)
```

### Step 3.1.4: Evaluate 1Q In-Sample Performance

```r
# Generate ensemble predictions
ensemble_pred_1q_train <- as.vector(X_train_1q %*% weights_1q)

# Calculate metrics
rmse_1q_train <- sqrt(mean((y_train_1q - ensemble_pred_1q_train)^2))
mae_1q_train <- mean(abs(y_train_1q - ensemble_pred_1q_train))
r2_1q_train <- cor(y_train_1q, ensemble_pred_1q_train)^2

cat("1Q In-Sample Performance:\n")
cat("  RMSE:", rmse_1q_train, "\n")
cat("  MAE :", mae_1q_train, "\n")
cat("  R²  :", r2_1q_train, "\n")
```

## ENSEMBLE 2: 6-Month Horizon

```r
cat("\n=== CREATING 6-MONTH ENSEMBLE ===\n")
```

```r
weights_6m <- lsei_6m$X

```

# PART 4: COMPARE WEIGHTS ACROSS HORIZONS

```r
cat("\n=== WEIGHT COMPARISON ACROSS HORIZONS ===\n")

weights_comparison <- data.frame(
  Model = c("RF", "XGBoost", "PCR"),
  Weight_1Q = weights_1q,
  Weight_6M = weights_6m,
  Weight_1Y = weights_1y
)

print(weights_comparison)

# Visualize
library(tidyr)
weights_long <- weights_comparison %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = starts_with("Weight_"), 
               names_to = "Horizon", 
               values_to = "Weight") %>%
  mutate(Horizon = gsub("Weight_", "", Horizon))

ggplot(weights_long, aes(x = Model, y = Weight, fill = Horizon)) +
  geom_col(position = "dodge") +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.1f%%", Weight * 100)),
            position = position_dodge(width = 0.9),
            vjust = -0.5, size = 3) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent_format()) +
  labs(title = "Ensemble Weights by Forecasting Horizon",
       subtitle = "Learned via LSEI on training data",
       y = "Weight", fill = "Horizon") +
  theme_minimal()
```

# PART 5: APPLY TO TEST SET

## Step 5.1: Load Test Predictions

```r
cat("\n=== LOADING TEST PREDICTIONS ===\n")

# Load test data (same structure as training)
rf_test <- read_csv("rf_test_predictions.csv") %>%
  select(date, 
         actual_1q, actual_6m, actual_1y,
         rf_forecast_1q, rf_forecast_6m, rf_forecast_1y)

xgb_test <- read_csv("xgb_test_predictions.csv") %>%
  select(date,
         xgb_forecast_1q, xgb_forecast_6m, xgb_forecast_1y)

pcr_test <- read_csv("pcr_test_predictions.csv") %>%
  select(date,
         pcr_forecast_1q, pcr_forecast_6m, pcr_forecast_1y)

# Combine
test_combined <- rf_test %>%
  left_join(xgb_test, by = "date") %>%
  left_join(pcr_test, by = "date")
```

## Step 5.2: Generate Ensemble Predictions (All Horizons)

```r
cat("\n=== GENERATING ENSEMBLE TEST PREDICTIONS ===\n")

# ===== 1-QUARTER ENSEMBLE PREDICTIONS =====
X_test_1q <- test_combined %>%
  select(rf_forecast_1q, xgb_forecast_1q, pcr_forecast_1q) %>%
  as.matrix()

ensemble_pred_1q_test <- as.vector(X_test_1q %*% weights_1q)

# ===== 6-MONTH ENSEMBLE PREDICTIONS =====
X_test_6m <- test_combined %>%
  select(rf_forecast_6m, xgb_forecast_6m, pcr_forecast_6m) %>%
  as.matrix()

ensemble_pred_6m_test <- as.vector(X_test_6m %*% weights_6m)

# ===== 1-YEAR ENSEMBLE PREDICTIONS =====
X_test_1y <- test_combined %>%
  select(rf_forecast_1y, xgb_forecast_1y, pcr_forecast_1y) %>%
  as.matrix()

ensemble_pred_1y_test <- as.vector(X_test_1y %*% weights_1y)

# Add to test dataframe
test_combined$ensemble_forecast_1q <- ensemble_pred_1q_test
test_combined$ensemble_forecast_6m <- ensemble_pred_6m_test
test_combined$ensemble_forecast_1y <- ensemble_pred_1y_test
```

## Step 5.3: Evaluate Out-of-Sample Performance

```r
cat("\n=== OUT-OF-SAMPLE PERFORMANCE ===\n\n")

# ===== 1Q HORIZON =====
rmse_1q_test <- sqrt(mean((test_combined$actual_1q - ensemble_pred_1q_test)^2))
mae_1q_test <- mean(abs(test_combined$actual_1q - ensemble_pred_1q_test))
r2_1q_test <- cor(test_combined$actual_1q, ensemble_pred_1q_test)^2

cat("1-Quarter Horizon:\n")
cat("  RMSE:", rmse_1q_test, "\n")
cat("  MAE :", mae_1q_test, "\n")
cat("  R²  :", r2_1q_test, "\n\n")

# ===== 6M HORIZON =====
rmse_6m_test <- sqrt(mean((test_combined$actual_6m - ensemble_pred_6m_test)^2))
mae_6m_test <- mean(abs(test_combined$actual_6m - ensemble_pred_6m_test))
r2_6m_test <- cor(test_combined$actual_6m, ensemble_pred_6m_test)^2

cat("6-Month Horizon:\n")
cat("  RMSE:", rmse_6m_test, "\n")
cat("  MAE :", mae_6m_test, "\n")
cat("  R²  :", r2_6m_test, "\n\n")

# ===== 1Y HORIZON =====
rmse_1y_test <- sqrt(mean((test_combined$actual_1y - ensemble_pred_1y_test)^2))
mae_1y_test <- mean(abs(test_combined$actual_1y - ensemble_pred_1y_test))
r2_1y_test <- cor(test_combined$actual_1y, ensemble_pred_1y_test)^2

cat("1-Year Horizon:\n")
cat("  RMSE:", rmse_1y_test, "\n")
cat("  MAE :", mae_1y_test, "\n")
cat("  R²  :", r2_1y_test, "\n\n")
```

```r
)
```

```r
# In strategy_backtest.Rmd, you would load:

ensemble_forecasts <- read_csv("../data/ensemble_predictions_multihorizon.csv")

# Then use:
# - ensemble_forecast_1q for quarterly rebalancing strategy
# - ensemble_forecast_6m for semi-annual rebalancing strategy
# - ensemble_forecast_1y for annual rebalancing strategy

# Example:
tactical_strategy_quarterly <- function(data) {
  data %>%
    mutate(position = ifelse(ensemble_forecast_1q > tbill_rate_3m, 
                             "SP500", "TBILL"))
}

tactical_strategy_semiannual <- function(data) {
  data %>%
    mutate(position = ifelse(ensemble_forecast_6m > tbill_rate_6m, 
                             "SP500", "TBILL"))
}

tactical_strategy_annual <- function(data) {
  data %>%
    mutate(position = ifelse(ensemble_forecast_1y > tbill_rate_1y, 
                             "SP500", "TBILL"))
}
```

# COMPLETE WORKFLOW SUMMARY

```
1. DATA LOADING
   ├── Load RF predictions (1q, 6m, 1y)
   ├── Load XGBoost predictions (1q, 6m, 1y)
   └── Load PCR predictions (1q, 6m, 1y)

2. TRAINING (3 SEPARATE ENSEMBLES)
   ├── ENSEMBLE 1: Learn weights for 1Q forecasts
   │   ├── Prepare X_train_1q matrix (RF, XGB, PCR forecasts)
   │   ├── Set up constraints (sum=1, all>=0)
   │   ├── Solve LSEI → weights_1q
   │   └── Evaluate in-sample performance
   │
   ├── ENSEMBLE 2: Learn weights for 6M forecasts
   │   ├── Prepare X_train_6m matrix
   │   ├── Set up constraints
   │   ├── Solve LSEI → weights_6m
   │   └── Evaluate in-sample performance
   │
   └── ENSEMBLE 3: Learn weights for 1Y forecasts
       ├── Prepare X_train_1y matrix
       ├── Set up constraints
       ├── Solve LSEI → weights_1y
       └── Evaluate in-sample performance

3. TESTING (APPLY 3 ENSEMBLES)
   ├── Load test predictions (1q, 6m, 1y from each model)
   ├── Apply weights_1q to get ensemble_forecast_1q
   ├── Apply weights_6m to get ensemble_forecast_6m
   ├── Apply weights_1y to get ensemble_forecast_1y
   └── Evaluate out-of-sample performance

4. SAVE OUTPUTS
   ├── ensemble_predictions_multihorizon.csv
   ├── ensemble_weights_multihorizon.csv
   └── ensemble_performance_summary.csv

5. USE IN BACKTESTING
   ├── Quarterly strategy uses ensemble_forecast_1q
   ├── Semi-annual strategy uses ensemble_forecast_6m
   └── Annual strategy uses ensemble_forecast_1y
```

---

# KEY INSIGHTS

1. **Different Weights Per Horizon**: Each horizon gets its own set of weights
   - Example: XGBoost might get 80% weight for 1Q, but only 40% for 1Y
   - This reflects different model strengths at different time scales

2. **Independent Optimization**: Each ensemble is learned independently
   - 1Q ensemble minimizes 1Q forecast errors
   - 6M ensemble minimizes 6M forecast errors
   - 1Y ensemble minimizes 1Y forecast errors

3. **Alignment with Strategies**: 
   - Quarterly rebalancing uses 1Q ensemble
   - Semi-annual rebalancing uses 6M ensemble
   - Annual rebalancing uses 1Y ensemble
   
4. **Data Requirements**: Need multi-horizon predictions from ALL base models
   - If a model only provides 1Q forecasts, it can't be included in 6M/1Y ensembles
   - All models must provide all 3 horizons for this to work
